Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is ready to move but we hit two items on the Order Form we need clarified before legal will sign:

1) Invoice recipient: OrbitOne has two billing entities. We need to confirm whether Redwood will invoice the US operating entity (OrbitOne, Inc.) or OrbitOne Global (Panama). For tax reasons they'd prefer the US entity if possible.

2) Minimum commit phasing: OrbitOne proposes smoothing the 12-month min commit into quarterly tranches tied to invoicing dates instead of an upfront single invoice. Can you confirm Redwood can accept tranche invoicing with a single Order Form and the net-terms applied per invoice? If there are any implications for SLA credits or proration, please spell those out.

Attaching a PO and a tracked Order Form with our minimal redlines.

Subject: Re: Redwood Order Form Qs — invoice recipient & timing

Alice — thanks for the note and the attachments. Quick responses below and then I'll loop in Ben and Kim for the legal/billing details.

1) Invoice recipient: Redwood can route invoices to OrbitOne, Inc. (US) as the primary invoicing entity. We'll need a signed Order Form that includes the billing entity name and W-9 or tax residency evidence for the US entity. If OrbitOne later requests a change to the recipient entity, we treat that as a contract amendment (standard).

2) Min-commit phasing: We can support tranche invoicing (quarterly) for the 12-month minimum commitment. Operationally:
- Each tranche invoice will carry the same net-terms (Net 30 by default unless otherwise requested).
- SLA credits and proration: credits accrue against the account, but entitlement math is computed on the full-year committed quantity; if you draw less than the annual committed tokens, credits do not create additional invoice reversals — we do reconciliations at each quarter and true-up at year-end if needed.

Ben/ Kim — can you confirm the legal language we should accept and whether we need an amendment to the MSA for tranche payment wording? Also flag any tax evidence we should collect before we route the first invoice to OrbitOne, Inc.

I'll schedule a short call if that helps.

— Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Looping in legal details.

Kimberly — proposed approach: accept the tranche invoicing in the Order Form appendix with the following bullets added to the Order Form (tracked in attached doc):
- Payment schedule: 4 equal quarterly invoices representing the annual minimum commit; each invoice due Net 30 from invoice date.
- True-up: At the end of the 12-month term Redwood will compare actual usage to committed usage; any shortfall will be invoiced as a final true-up invoice due Net 30.
- SLA impact: SLA credits are calculated on actual performance and applied as account-level credit; they do not reduce the minimum commit invoice amounts except via the final true-up reconciliation.
- Tax & entity evidence: Prior to first invoice Redwood requires a completed tax residency form (W-9 for US entity) and the billing entity name on the signed Order Form.

Kim — are any redlines required on the MSA to permit quarterly invoicing? My read: no core MSA change is necessary; keep it in the Order Form appendix as commercial terms to avoid MSA churn. If legal prefers, we can add a short amendment clause referencing payment schedule changes.

Alice — if that sounds good, Kimberly will confirm redline language and we'll produce a clean Order Form + short amendment clause for signature.

Cheers,
